h: Making the most of a Cheltenham night out
p: Coming in for the racing? During the March Festival, Cheltenham is rammed with visitors, and anything with a bar and a bit of entertainment gets snapped up fast. If you're planning a post-racing game of bowling, book your lane well ahead and expect a lively crowd. The rest of the year, weekend evenings are the busy times, while midweek is usually more relaxed.

Before you go, bring photo ID if you look young, as bar-led venues commonly ask for it. Think about lane numbers too: four to six players per lane keeps the game moving, while bigger groups are better off over two lanes. Agree on teams and a forfeit before the first ball, and swap players around halfway through to keep things fair.

The High Street is a handy base. Cheltenham Spa station is a short bus ride or a longer walk away, and there are plenty of buses running along the main roads. Right nearby, the Brewery Quarter has restaurants and a cinema if you fancy a full evening out, and the Regent Arcade's quirky Wishing Fish Clock is a fun little stop for anyone who hasn't seen it.

For a show before or after, the Everyman Theatre on Regent Street is a gorgeous Victorian playhouse hosting everything from drama to panto. Combined with a few frames and some food, it makes for a cracking night in one of the Cotswolds' liveliest towns.
